newsitem.title: MEXICO: Emerging markets rebounded in 1996 - Robleda.
newsitem.headline: Emerging markets rebounded in 1996 - Robleda.

text.p: Emerging market stock markets rebounded smartly in 1996, posting a 5.8 percent return, Manuel Robleda, president of the International Federation of Stock Exchanges, said on Tuesday.
"Nineteen ninety-six was a good year for emerging markets, as they fully recovered from 1994, a year of turbulence," Robleda told an international conference on emerging markets.
The largest gain was posted among Latin American stock markets, which showed a 14.0 percent hike in 1996, Robleda, also chairman of the Mexican bolsa, said.
The second largest gain was an 8.9 percent increase in Asian markets, he noted.
Other emerging markets showed an average 5.2 percent decline last year, he said.
Robleda said greater market services are being offered in these emerging markets, and an increased number of financial products such as securities lending and short-selling.
He said a positive sign was an increase in capital flows, with $45.7 billion in new money flowing into emerging markets in 1996, the first annual increase since 1993.
The larger portfolio flows were due to a number of factors, including better risk perception, attractive valuations and greater access, particularly with depository receipts, Robleda said.
He said there are now 556 depository receipts from 42 different nations.
